text:
The Oilers are 12-3-3 and the headlines are what you'd expect: Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard joining an exclusive list, Draisaitl scoring at the best rate of his career at 31 (per Squawka), and a standing ovation for Ryan Nugent-Hopkins after he set a team record. Saturday's 4-2 win over Vancouver had Draisaitl finishing off McDavid feeds and Jason Dickinson scoring in his revenge game.

Now the uncomfortable part. Edmonton has scored 19.4 more goals than its chances predict, a gap that size almost never holds, and at five on five it takes 49 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Our race model thinks the Oilers have banked about 5.7 more points than their play deserved. That's money in the bank, and they keep it, but it isn't a habit you can count on.

The top line, Draisaitl, McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin, has outscored teams 18-6 and is the whole engine. Behind it, the Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line has 35 percent of the expected goals, and the Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea pair carries big minutes on the wrong side of the chances. Isaac Howard is out a couple of weeks. Devon Levi's return in net is the piece to watch.
headline: Edmonton's record is real. The margin under it isn't.
